https://www.eyeradio.org/un-security-cou.text: About us Careers Contact Us Listen Live You are here: Home | Justice | News | Peace | Security | UN Security Council: France, Latvia demand release of Dr Riek Machar and immediate dialogue UN Security Council: France, Latvia demand release of Dr Riek Machar and immediate dialogue Author: Staff reporter | Published: August 8, 2026 Share with friends: Dr Riek Machar, Leader of SPLM-IO Representatives from France and Latvia at the United Nations called on South Sudan to release suspended First Vice President Dr. Riek Machar and all political detainees during a UN Security Council session on the country’s ongoing transition. Addressing the Council during its 10,206th meeting, diplomats from both nations warned that the ongoing political impasse and detention of opposition leaders threaten peace and stability ahead of planned national elections. The representative of France characterized the political landscape in South Sudan as highly unstable, expressing concern over the continued legal proceedings and detention of key political figures despite regional appeals. “The political situation in the country remains tense and precarious,” the French delegate stated. “We note that the calls from the African Union to lift proceedings against persons detained for political reasons, including First Vice President Riek Machar, have not been heeded. We once again call upon the South Sudanese authorities to follow up on this.” France reiterated that a return to genuine, inclusive dialogue among signatories of the 2018 Revitalized Peace Agreement is the only viable path toward completing the democratic transition safely. In her address, the Permanent Representative of Latvia to the UN, Ambassador Sanita Pavļuta-Deslandes, emphasized that urgent confidence-building measures are needed to prevent widespread escalation before, during, and after the upcoming polls. “We urge the authorities to engage in a genuine and inclusive high-level dialogue, rebuild consensus and agree on the safeguards needed to ensure peaceful, inclusive, free and fair elections,” Ambassador Pavļuta-Deslandes said. “We also call for the release of First Vice President Riek Machar and other political detainees as an urgent confidence-building measure. Addressing these gaps is essential to prevent violence before, during and after the elections.” Latvia further cautioned against unilateral actions that bypass agreed peace framework procedures, warning that eroding political trust jeopardizes the integrity of the entire transitional period. https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: Hawk wildfire in Nevada forces evacuations and road closures US wildfires Fast-moving wildfire in Reno, Nevada, forces tens of thousands to evacuate homes Human-caused Hawk fire covers more than 15,000 acres as blaze approaches University of Nevada campus in Reno Marina Dunbar and agencies Sun 23 Aug 2026 14.22 EDT Last modified on Sun 23 Aug 2026 19.59 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A fast-moving Nevada wildfire exploded to more than 15,000 acres (6,000 hectares) on Sunday, pushing from the Sierra foothills toward the center of Reno and urging nearly 90,000 residents to evacuate as flames threatened neighborhoods and reached the edge of the University of Nevada campus. The Hawk fire’s “GO NOW” evacuation zone had expanded to the edge of the university campus as strong, gusty winds, low humidity and dry vegetation fueled the blaze, according to Truckee Meadows Fire and Rescue in Reno. Of those urged to evacuate, 42,000 were under strict orders. An additional 45,000 people were in the evacuation warning zone, and encouraged to leave now and be prepared to stay away for several days to clear the roads for first-responders. “If you have been told to evacuate, please don’t wait!” Hillary Schieve, Reno’s mayor, said in a statement posted on social media on Saturday night. “Structures have already been burned in this fire and your life is more important than a building. Evacuating before the fire arrives also allows our firefighters to focus their efforts on battling the blaze.” Firefighters sound alarm as US faces critical staffing shortage: ‘We don’t have enough people’ Read more Authorities confirmed three civilians and three first responders had been injured in the fire and several structures have been destroyed. Officials said the fire was human-caused but did not provide additional details on how the fire was started, saying it was under investigation. Governor Joe Lombardo declared a state of emergency in Washoe county and mobilized the Nevada national guard. Two helicopter crews were deployed to support aerial firefighting operations, while 60 troops were assigned to help police safeguard evacuated neighborhoods. However winds were whipping the flames, complicating the fight. “It was extremely confusing,” said Darin Balaam, the Washoe county sheriff, describing how changing winds sent the flames in different directions. The fire had already proved to be a challenge on Saturday night, moving exceptionally fast, jumping over fire trucks and making it difficult for responders to get to hotspots while residents were trying to get out, Balaam said. The fire was so small on Saturday morning that it wasn’t even a concern, said Tyler Duvall, who went camping over the weekend. By the next day, his house was in the evacuation zone. “The wind really blew it up,” Duvall said. “Approximately 400 personnel are currently working on the incident, with resources coming together from local, state and federal agencies, including ground crews and air resources,” the Truckee Meadows statement said. The rapidly expanding fire was surrounded by neighborhoods, and nearly 10,000 homes and businesses in Washoe county were without power on Sunday. Portions of US Route 395, a major north-south highway, were closed because of the fire. Reno has a population of more than 280,000 residents. View image in fullscreen Fire crews and local agencies respond to a fast-moving wildfire on the dry hillsides outside Reno, Nevada, on Saturday. Photograph: Hale Irwin/NurPhoto/Shutterstock David Barb returned from a weekend hunting trip to find the fire had leveled his taxidermy shop, but his house nearby appeared to have been spared thanks to workers with a landscaping company who cut a fire break, he said. His wife was home when the fire started on the other side of the mountain and later evacuated to a friend’s house. “I’m kind of devastated, but thank God everyone’s safe,” he said on Sunday. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Around 2-3 times a day Sign up to Breaking News US Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion Washoe county emergency officials opened the Reno-Sparks Convention Center to evacuees, but said pets could not be brought there. Small and large animals were instead to be left at two other locations. Casinos in Reno offered discounts on hotel rooms to evacuees. At least 20 road closures were in effect as of Sunday afternoon. The University of Nevada’s Reno campus remained just outside the evacuation zone on Sunday morning. The university, which had an enrollment of about 24,000 students in fall 2025, said officials had established an emergency response plan should conditions change. The first day of classes at the university is 24 August. However, students who are new to the university were allowed to move in as early as 13 August. The Reno-Tahoe international airport also remained outside the evacuation zone, and commercial flights were unaffected on Sunday. The smaller Reno-Stead airport was closed to general aviation traffic because of the Hawk fire but remained open to firefighting aircraft. Authorities were also closely watching a county detention facility located several blocks from the outer edge of the evacuation warning area. “We have those inmates in mind and we are making sure that we have plans in place in case we may have to evacuate the facility,” said Darin Balaam, the Washoe county sheriff. The Hawk fire comes just weeks after three wildfires fueled by dry and windy conditions north of Reno forced more than 13,000 residents from their homes earlier this month, according to the Nevada national guard. https://www.politico.eu/article/tories-a.text: LONDON — The architects of Britain's first post-Brexit trade deals have warned that the country's independent trade policy is under threat after Andy Burnham pledged a major review of the country’s relationship with the EU. Their intervention marks the latest salvo in a political fightback against Burnham's EU policy as the Conservative Party conference gets underway in Birmingham this weekend. Burnham this week vowed to discuss a revamped relationship with Europe, including rejoining the EU's customs union, moving closer the bloc's single market — or even pushing to outright rejoin the bloc . It marks a fundamental shift from a Labour Party that has previously ruled out all three. Advertisement Advertisement Customs union membership — a popular option among some members of Burnham’s Cabinet — would ease trade between the U.K. and its largest trading partner, but require Britain to sacrifice the trade deals it has struck since leaving the bloc six years ago. Greg Hands, who served as trade minister four times between 2016 to 2024 under Conservative governments, said that all options presented “grave consequences for Britain's independent trade policy.” “Depending exactly on what is agreed, it is likely to invalidate or make very difficult most — if not all — of those existing trade agreements, or many of those existing trade agreements,” he said. Since Brexit, the U.K. has negotiated free trade deals with nations including Australia, New Zealand, Japan and — more recently — the Asia Pacific trading bloc CPTPP, India, the Gulf states, as well as upgraded deals with South Korea and Switzerland. Although the U.K. could technically copy-and paste EU versions of trade deals, Hands warned that the terms might not be so favorable, highlighting that the U.K.-Japan deal he had helped to negotiate “has got much more liberal rules on data” than the EU equivalent. As a non-EU member, the U.K. would also surrender its ability to negotiate the terms of any new trade deals, Hands argued. “Why would the EU prioritize the U.K., which is not a paying member of the EU, over paying full members of the EU when it does trade agreements?” Advertisement Advertisement But the issue goes further than free trade agreements, he said, pointing out that entering a customs union with the EU would affect the U.K.’s global tariff — the independent system of taxes and duty rates applied to goods imported from other countries. This would be a “huge diminution of the U.K.'s influence in the world to align or take the EU's customs tariff,” Hands added. Moreover, by signing up to a customs union, the U.K. would also lose its ability to erect its own trade defenses and be forced to implement EU measures like tariffs on steel and electric vehicles, Hands warned. He also cautioned that closer alignment could complicate relations with the U.S., which has been critical of U.K. ambitions for closer alignment with the EU. “The U.S. is our single largest bilateral trading partner and I don’t think it would be in the U.K.’s interest to mess up that relationship.” End of CPTPP membership Liam Fox, a self-proclaimed “staunch euroskeptic” who served as trade secretary in the immediate aftermath of the referendum, between 2016 and 2019, said rejoining the EU or customs union would “mean an end to Britain’s independent trade policy and any strategy influence we have from membership of organizations such as [the Asia-Pacific trade bloc] CPTPP.” “This vague language from Andy Burnham is all about keeping the Labour left quiet whatever the consequences,” Fox added. “Rejoining the EU would mean being part of Schengen with free movement of people and adoption of the Euro. If that is what Andy Burnham wants, let him make the case for it, stop his mealy-mouthed pandering to his own party and start acting like a real prime minister.” A third former Tory trade minister — granted anonymity to speak frankly — told MTUK the risks to Britain’s new trade deals was “real” and would “undermine new relationships with some of the fastest growing middle-class economies in the world.” “As the mature EU markets continue to be a smaller part of U.K. export opportunities, the prime minister should be focusing on supporting U.K. businesses to win export contracts where huge new markets exist,” the former minister argued.
